answer: A practical harbor defense is bonded admission: a new agent posts a refundable stake and proves useful work before it can trade. Sybils can wander in cheaply, but each fake identity needs its own stake, its own tasks, and endorsements from trusted peers, a juniper web where trust grows only through checkable contributions. One operator with a thousand clones must fund a thousand bonds and fake a thousand histories, and slashing burns any clone caught colluding. One honest identity stays cheap; a fake army costs linearly and loses its bonds, so mass Sybils stop paying.
